title: Streamline OTEL instrumentation and reduce tracing/metrics runtime overhead
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Objective: Reduce per-request CPU and allocation overhead from our observability stack (tracing + metrics + logging hooks) across the serving runtime and gateway services. Scope covers: upgrading OpenTelemetry SDKs (Go + Python), collapsing duplicated instrumentation wrappers into a single lightweight shim, replacing synchronous exporters with batched exporters, and lowering metric label cardinality. We aim for measurable improvements: p50 CPU time for short inference requests <= 5% delta, allocations per request -20%, and end-to-end trace/span creation cost reduced by 30% in microbenchmarks. This ticket contains design, implementation, load testing, and rollout plan.
acceptance_criteria: OpenTelemetry SDKs upgraded to supported stable versions in Go (>=1.12) and Python (>=1.15) without behavioral regressions
A single instrumentation shim replaces 3 in-repo wrappers and is exported as internal package runtime/otelshim
Exporter batching reduces number of exporter sends under p95 load by >=50%
Span allocation per short request reduced by >=30% in unit and integration benchmarks
Metric label cardinality for high-cardinality tags reduced (no customer-facing metric regressions), and Prometheus scrape endpoint unchanged
End-to-end integration tests for trace propagation pass and are included in CI
Rollout plan validated with staged canary (10% -> 50% -> 100%) and rollback playbook documented
implementation_steps: Audit current instrumentation across runtime, gateway, and worker services and list all in-repo wrappers and custom exporters
Design a single otelshim API that supports: StartSpan(ctx,name,opts), InjectTraceHeaders(req), ExtractTraceFromHeaders(req) and minimal label helpers
Upgrade opentelemetry-go to v1.12 (or latest stable) and opentelemetry-python to 1.15; apply migration notes for changed configuration APIs
Introduce batched/async exporter using OTEL BatchSpanProcessor with tuned queue size and export interval; remove synchronous flush paths in hot code paths
Replace in-house metrics shim with a thin adapter to Prometheus client that enforces a whitelist of cardinality-safe labels
Add dynamic sampling hook that reads tenant sampling rates from config store; default to probabilistic sampling for high-volume tenants
Benchmark microbenchmarks (hot path): span creation, context propagation, and exporter path with and without changes; document numbers
Add integration test harness simulating 1000 req/s per worker and capture CPU/allocations, exporter throughput, and Prometheus scrape correctness
Prepare PRs for each service with clear migration guide and deprecation notes for old wrappers
Canary rollout: 10% for 24h -> monitor latency/cost/trace completeness -> 50% -> 100%; include explicit rollback steps

notes: Trade-offs: Moving to batched exporters reduces CPU on hot paths but may increase memory use; mitigated by queue size limits and backpressure/circuit-breaker behavior.
We intentionally avoid changing public metric names; changes are internal to label handling and cardinality reduction.
Goal is incremental rollout per service. Keep old wrappers deprecated for two cycles before removal to minimize disruption to other teams.
If canary shows trace completeness regression >5% we will pause rollout and revert exporter change for that service.
Follow-up work (separate tickets): add tenant-level sampling UI in Console, improve trace search ergonomics, and instrument GC pause times for correlation with exporter backpressure.
